items.title: a HANDLE STUB inside a COLD select re-mints per PULL: `get_client().and_then(\|client\| client.get_channels()).map(..).cell()` — the shape the Order 40 census prescribed as `map_safe`'s replacement, at all seven kolt model.vl sites — reads `[]` forever. `AndThen::get` re-runs `select` on every pull and a generated stub (`unleased_source`, rpc.vl:5941) mints a FRESH unleased mirror per call, so `.cell()`'s refresh (`cached.set(self.get())`) reads a mirror nothing ever leased (`None`) while the leased one — the one `on_settle`'s `follow` picked — lives on in the registration. The wire, the server and the wake are all correct; the value is read off the wrong object
items.discussion: kolt 2026-09-28; repro `sweeps/order43/probes/kolt-mirrors/` (A = kolt's shape reads 0/0/0, B = the stub called once reads 0/1/2, C/D/E = the `.cell()` idiom on all three stub forms read 0/1/2); the flip's `AndThen` (reactive.vl:2013) vs A92's per-call mint; the same census that wrote the shape (`sweeps/order40/reactive-40/kolt_census_2026-09-22.md`)
items.body:
Mechanism, in order: `.cell()` reads `self.get()` once (select → mirror #1, unleased, `None`), then `on_settle` → `AndThen::on_settle`'s `follow` (select → mirror #2, leased: `Subscribe`, seed, forward), then each settle wakes the cell and its refresh calls `self.get()` again (select → mirror #3, unleased, `None`). Every pull is a fresh mint; the push path and the pull path never meet the same mirror. Pure selects are unaffected — the trap is a select with an EFFECT, and a sync stub is exactly that, by design (A92: "an app that mints a hundred handles and renders ten makes TEN calls").

Kolt's fix (applied 2026-09-28 at the seven model.vl sites, checks/builds/fmt clean): pin the mirror under a cell of its own between the `map` and the `and_then` — `get_client().map(|c| c.map(|c| c.get_channels())).cell().and_then(|mirror| mirror).map(..).cell()` — so the select is the identity and the one mirror the client made is what every pull reads.

Doors for std: (a) the generated client DEDUPS mirrors per ORIGIN (method + described args) — the client twin of A92's server-side identity dedup; a second stub call for the same origin hands back the same mirror, so a select that mints is idempotent and the census's shape simply works. Cost: a per-client table keyed by the origin's serialized args, released with the mirror's last lease (or with the connection). (b) `AndThen`/`Switch`/`FlattenOption::get` read the FOLLOWED inner while a subscriber is attached (the node keeps `inner` in its registration already) — but a cold node that answers differently attached vs unattached is a new kind of node, against A124's letter. (c) document the idiom above at the stub's doc (rpc.vl:5900) and remote-sources.md, and rewrite the census's two sites. Rec: (a) + (c); (a) also makes kolt's hand `Memo` tables optional. Sizing S–M; std/rpc, Order 43.

items.title: an `[rpc]` body that returns `field.map(..).cell()` (kolt store.vl:197/206/258 after the flip's `.cell()` edits) mints a FRESH derived cell per CALL: A92's `expose_dynamic` dedup keys on `cell_identity`, so it never hits — one capability, one forward and one copy of every update per `Subscribe` for a value the connection already carries; and the dispatcher runs handlers under NO ambient owner, so the cell's `register_with_owner` keeps its upstream subscription on the module-level store cell for the PROCESS — a leaked subscription per call, growing with every re-lease and reconnect (`reattach_mirrors` re-issues the call). Not new to the flip (the pre-flip `map` was per-call too) but now written out in every migrated service
items.discussion: kolt 2026-09-28; the in-process probe `sweeps/order43/probes/kolt-mirrors/` prints `server: get_channels called` once per variant, each a new cell; A92 (dedup by identity); A28 (owner-optional `.cell()`); C14's leak gate would count these on native
items.body: Doors: (a) the SERVICE memoizes the derived cell per (method, args) — a `Memo` field on the store, which kolt's `users: Memo<UserId, SignalCell<Option<User>>>` already does for `get_user` and which A134's door (a) mirrors client-side; document it as the rule for a handle-returning `[rpc]` ("return a cell that OUTLIVES the call"). (b) the dispatcher runs each handler under the CONNECTION's owner (`Service::factory` has the seam: the instance is dropped with the connection), so a per-call cell dies with the connection instead of the process — bounds the leak, does not restore the dedup. (c) a check: a handle-returning `[rpc]` whose tail is a `.cell()` (or any derivation constructor) gets a warning with the memo steer — static, cheap, catches every migrated site. Rec: (b) + (c) now, (a) as the documented idiom. Sizing S (b, c) / doc (a); std/rpc + the analyzer's service expansion, Order 43.
